review_notes: I read all 51 lines. The file has two theorems, `aux` and `solution`, and no definitions, structures, instances or simp attributes. It adds no `@[simp]` lemmas and no simp sets. The proofs use explicit `rw`, `show` and `exact`. They use existing Mathlib lemmas (`Fin.succ_last`, `Fin.castSucc_zero`, `Matrix.cons_val_succ`, `Matrix.cons_val_zero`, `Fin.succ_castSucc`). The file introduces no rewrite direction, competing rules, unwanted expansion or cycle. The only possible simp-related point is that the `rw` chains could be replaced by `simp`. That would be a proof-style choice and not a defect in a simp interface. The theorem statements are existential chain statements, not normal-form rewrite rules, so a simp attribute on them would not be justified. I did not search the rest of the repository for downstream uses, because the file adds no simp-relevant declaration for such a search to check.
